newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia, China agree on human rights dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Australia, China agree on human rights dialogue.

text.p: Australia said on Thursday it had reached agreement with China for the two countries to establish a formal "bilateral dialogue on human rights".

Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said the agreement, reached in principle with visiting Chinese Justice Minister Xiao Yang on Wednesday, would help achieve progress on human rights in China.

"While there will inevitably be differences between Australia and China on human rights issues, a formal bilateral dialogue will provide a framework for dealing with such differences and for pursuing concrete improvement in the observance of internationally-recognised human rights standards in China," Downer said in a statement.

The timing and details of the human rights dialogue, suggested by Australian Prime Minister John Howard to Chinese counterpart Li Peng in Beijing last week, will be thrashed out by officials in the coming weeks.

The news comes amid international diplomatic tension over a draft resolution at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva censuring China for human rights abuses. The draft resolution has been proposed by Denmark and has U.S. backing.
Australia, keen to mend relations with China after a year of minor spats, has not yet said whether it will support the Danish motion.
